A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FRT and Conformal Selective Borrowing study, with matching authors, clinical application, and substantial retained material. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations and an analysis combining CALGB 9633 trial data with NCDB external controls, including additional simulation results in Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 reports revised simulations, additional empirical analyses in Appendix C, and the CALGB 9633–NCDB clinical analysis.

M1.justification: The adaptive threshold algorithm changes substantially. V1 Section 3.2 estimates MSE through repeated two-fold splitting; v3 Section 3.3 and Algorithm 1 instead use the full-sample squared difference from the no-borrowing estimator, subtract its bootstrap-estimated variance, and add the borrowing estimator's bootstrap variance. The underlying FRT and four conformal variants remain; full conformal and jackknife+ move to Appendix A.

E1.justification: V3 changes the main simulated covariate population from two-dimensional normal covariates to uniform covariates on [-2, 2], and adds a five-dimensional correlated Gaussian scenario in Appendix C.6. The hybrid-trial task and CALGB 9633–NCDB clinical population remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The NB, FB, and ALSB point-estimator comparators are retained. ALSB newly participates in type I error and power comparisons using asymptotic inference, and v3 Figure 7 compares NB, ALSB, and CSB under asymptotic inference. V1 evaluated ALSB's estimation and selection performance but omitted its testing results. FB is also omitted from the corresponding fixed-threshold comparison plots in v3.

E3.justification: V3 adds an effect-size sweep for power curves at hidden-bias magnitudes 0 and 8 and introduces explicit asymptotic-versus-FRT evaluation protocols. The false-selection-rate metric reported in v1 is dropped. The principal sample sizes, 10-fold CV+, clinical preprocessing, and outcome definition remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds power-versus-effect-size curves, analyses comparing asymptotic inference with FRT, and robustness results for five dependent covariates. These substantially expand checks of power, calibration, and robustness. Conversely, v1's quantitative false-selection-rate analysis is removed, although selection scatterplots remain. Larger-EC-sample and fixed-threshold analyses were already present in v1.

E5.justification: V3 adds error bars to simulated type I error rates, including Figure 2 and appendix comparisons; v1 presents these rates without error bars. Their construction and coverage level are not explained. Both versions report 500 simulation replications and 5,000 FRT draws and provide asymptotic standard errors and confidence intervals for the clinical analysis.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes CSB's clinical estimate from 0.236 to 0.138, its confidence interval from (0.114, 0.359) to (0.024, 0.252), and its FRT p-value from 0.028 to 0.046. Selected controls change from 178 to 264 in the table, although v3's prose still says 178. Simulation results also change: the reported no-bias CSB power gain over NB rises from 38% to 45%, and new appendix results are added. Changed tuning and covariate generation prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V3 adds Theorems 3.4 and 3.5, establishing uniform MSE-estimation error and oracle excess squared-error bounds under sub-Gaussian assumptions, with proofs in Appendices B.7–B.8. V1 has no corresponding adaptive-selection guarantees. V3 also tightens the model-correctness condition used to infer the full-borrowing variance advantage. Earlier FRT and conformal results are largely retained.

C1.justification: The central claims of exact FRT type I error control and individualized conformal borrowing remain. V3 adds a prominent contribution claiming non-asymptotic guarantees for adaptive MSE-based threshold selection, while shifting emphasis away from presenting fixed and adaptive thresholds as parallel recommendations. Adaptive MSE selection itself was already proposed in v1.

C2.justification: V1 already explains power losses and borrowing trade-offs. V3 adds a rationale for optimizing MSE rather than family-wise error or false discovery rates, connects difficult-bias behavior to Hodges estimation and transferability detection, and explicitly discusses the absence of uniform improvement over RCT-only analysis. These refine existing interpretations rather than reverse them.

D1.justification: V1's clinical execution details—5,000 FRT iterations taking about 10 minutes on an eight-core MacBook—are omitted. The revised bootstrap algorithm specifies an input L without reporting its numerical value, whereas v1 specified 100 splitting repetitions. The intFRT repository disclosure and clinical preprocessing software information remain available; matching details move to Appendix D.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands the literature coverage and positioning around test-then-pool methods, Bayesian borrowing, control variates, and bias modeling. It adds connections to causal model selection, Hodges estimation, transferability costs, and regulatory guidance. Examples include Li et al. (2020), Schmidli et al. (2014), Rothenhäusler (2020), and Cai et al. (2024). The Gao ALSB citation's publication update is not a new comparator.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution narrative, method exposition, and discussion are extensively rewritten and compressed. Section 3 is reorganized around an estimator class and adaptive selection; full conformal and jackknife+ move to a new appendix section. Clinical matching details also move, and separate Software and Data and Impact Statement sections are introduced.

P2.justification: The manuscript changes from a spacious single-column format to a two-column conference main text. Figures are substantially recomposed: Figure 1 loses the CSB histogram row, performance and selection plots are merged, threshold boxplots are removed while histograms remain, and new comparison figures appear. Simulation axes and error-bar displays change, and the relocated clinical selection plot gains a shaded quantile-regression region.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens the previously unanalysed adaptive-selection component through an explicit revised criterion and non-asymptotic guarantees in Theorems 3.4–3.5. Added inference-calibration comparisons and correlated-covariate tests also better establish where the approach works and fails. These gains outweigh the loss of false-selection-rate diagnostics and some reproducibility details. However, undefined simulation error bars and the unresolved 264-versus-178 clinical control-count discrepancy remain material weaknesses. The improvement rests on stronger justification and validation, not higher reported performance.
